reasons: Both answers hit every rubric item: each says plainly to send tonight because today is the last day, neither offers the hour or office hours as a reason to wait, and both draft a complete placeholder-only notice naming the ceiling leak on the 3rd. A edges ahead on execution: it separates the timely notice from the later documentation explicitly, points to the email timestamp as proof of timeliness, warns against guessing the leak's cause, and states its non-expert limits without softening the recommendation. A's draft is also slightly fuller (policyholder block, mitigation, mailing address, date) and keeps the date of loss as a clean placeholder, where B's "[the 3rd — month, year]" is a clumsier field and its narrative line drops back to a generic full-date placeholder.
